name: tokenize_text
description: Split text into words and sentences, Unicode-aware, with counts, frequencies and code-point offsets. Words keep internal apostrophes and hyphens (l'homme, well-known, COVID-19); URLs, e-mail addresses and numbers (3.50, 1.000,5, +34, 12 %) stay single tokens; each Han, hiragana or katakana character is a token; sentence ends at . ! ? … and 。！？ skip the abbreviations of English, Spanish, French or German (Mr., Sr., Mme, z. B.), initials, dotted acronyms and German ordinals. A rule-based tokeniser, not a statistical one.

language.description: Chooses the abbreviation list for sentence ends

tokens.description: Include the token list with types and offsets

sentences.description: Include the sentence list with offsets

top.description: Most frequent words to list (0: none)

lowercase.description: Case-fold words for frequencies and the unique count

input.text: Dr. Smith paid $3.50 at https://example.com/a?b=1. He left... then came back!

catalog.source: original; word rules after Unicode UAX #29 (letters, marks and digits with internal apostrophes and hyphens), sentence rules after the Punkt-style abbreviation heuristics
